definition.val: A relation that gives the number of ligand molecules in a molecular system. A ligand here is a small molecule being studied for how it binds to a larger one. No field in a topology file records this, so it has to be stated by whoever describes the system. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that gives the number of ligand molecules in a system that carry a net electrical charge. It matters because charged ligands change how the system must be neutralised and how its electrostatics behave. No field in a topology file records this, so it has to be stated by whoever describes the system. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that gives the number of distinct shapes of a ligand being considered in a study. Docking and conformational analysis generate many shapes of the same molecule, and how many were kept affects what the result means. No field in a topology file records this, so it has to be stated by whoever describes the system. (UNVERIFIED)

nodes.lbl: number of total atoms in the largest residue

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of atoms in the biggest single residue of a system. A standard amino acid has fewer than 30, so a much larger figure marks a cofactor, a ligand or a modified residue. It is a quick way to notice that a system contains something other than a plain polymer. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The NMXRS pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of massless interaction sites in a molecular model, which carry charge or interaction parameters but sit at no nucleus. They let charge be placed where no atom is, such as on a lone pair or slightly off an oxygen. Four-point water models and halogen bonding parameters are the usual reason a system has any. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The NUMEXTRA pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

definition.val: A relation that groups properties quantifying the covalent structure and connectivity of a molecular system, such as the number of bonds, angles and dihedral angles. Together they describe the topology, which is the graph of how the atoms are joined. (UNVERIFIED)

nodes.lbl: number of total bonds with hydrogens

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of covalent bonds in a system in which one of the 2 atoms is a hydrogen. These bonds vibrate faster than anything else in the system, so they are usually held at a fixed length to permit a longer timestep. In an organic system they are roughly half of all bonds. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The NBONH pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

nodes.lbl: number of total bonds without hydrogens

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of covalent bonds in a system that join 2 heavy atoms, with no hydrogen involved. These bonds form the skeleton of each molecule and are not normally constrained, because they vibrate slowly enough for the timestep to follow them. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The MBONA pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

nodes.lbl: number of total angles with hydrogens

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of bond angles in a system in which at least one of the 3 atoms is a hydrogen. Angles involving hydrogen bend fastest, so some simulations constrain them as well as the bonds. Doing so permits a longer timestep still, at the cost of losing that motion. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The NTHETH pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

nodes.lbl: number of total angles without hydrogens

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of bond angles in a system formed entirely by heavy atoms. These angles set the shape of each molecule's skeleton and are almost never constrained. Bending them is the main way a molecule accommodates strain. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The MTHETA pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

nodes.lbl: number of total dihedral angles with hydrogens

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of dihedral angles in a system in which at least one of the 4 defining atoms is a hydrogen. Most of these describe the rotation of groups such as methyl and hydroxyl. They are numerous and individually unimportant, which is why they are counted separately from the rest. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The NPHIH pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

nodes.lbl: number of total dihedral angles without hydrogens

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of dihedral angles in a system defined entirely by heavy atoms. These are the rotations that decide what shapes a molecule can adopt, including the backbone angles of a protein. They carry most of what a force field knows about conformation. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The MPHIA pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

nodes.lbl: number of total excluded atom pairs

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of atom pairs whose non-bonded interaction is deliberately left out of the calculation. Atoms 1 or 2 bonds apart are excluded because the bonded terms already describe how they interact, and counting both would double the effect. The exclusion list is part of the topology rather than a setting. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The NNB pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

definition.val: A relation that groups properties counting the degrees of freedom held fixed during a simulation, such as the bonds and angles made rigid by an algorithm like SHAKE. They record how far the natural dynamics of the system has been altered. (UNVERIFIED)

nodes.lbl: number of total bonds with constraints

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of covalent bonds whose length is held fixed by a constraint algorithm during a simulation. Each constrained bond removes one degree of freedom from the system, which is why the figure is needed to compute temperature correctly. It is obtained by subtracting 2 counts in the topology rather than read from a single field. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: prmtop NBONA - MBONA

nodes.lbl: number of total angles with constraints

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of bond angles held fixed by a constraint algorithm during a simulation. Constraining angles as well as bonds permits a longer timestep and removes the motion being constrained. It is obtained by subtracting 2 counts in the topology rather than read from a single field. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: prmtop NTHETA - MTHETA

nodes.lbl: number of total dihedrals with constraints

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of dihedral angles held fixed by a constraint algorithm during a simulation. Constraining a dihedral prevents a rotation entirely, so it is done rarely and deliberately. It is obtained by subtracting 2 counts in the topology rather than read from a single field. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: prmtop NPHIA - MPHIA

definition.val: A relation that groups properties counting the distinct force field parameters applied to a molecular system, such as the number of unique bond, angle and atom types. The counts indicate how complex the energy function used to model the system is. (UNVERIFIED)

nodes.lbl: number of total unique bond types

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of different bond parameter sets a system's topology draws on. Two bonds share a type when the force field gives them the same preferred length and stiffness. The figure reflects how chemically varied the bonding in the system is, not how many bonds there are. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The NUMBND pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

nodes.lbl: number of total unique angle types

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of different angle parameter sets a system's topology draws on. Two angles share a type when the force field gives them the same preferred value and stiffness. The figure reflects the variety of local geometries the system contains. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The NUMANG pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

nodes.lbl: number of total unique dihedral types

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of different dihedral parameter sets a system's topology draws on. Dihedral parameters control which rotations are preferred, so this figure reflects how varied the conformational behaviour of the system is. It is usually the largest of the 3 parameter type counts. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The NPTRA pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

nodes.lbl: number of total atom types in the parameter file

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of atom types defined in the force field parameter files being used, rather than the number appearing in one system. It describes the coverage of the force field itself. A general-purpose organic force field defines far more than a protein force field does. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The NATYP pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

nodes.lbl: number of total distinct hydrogen bond pair types

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of distinct hydrogen bond parameter sets defined in a force field, for the older treatment that gives hydrogen bonds a potential of their own. Modern force fields describe hydrogen bonds through ordinary electrostatics and van der Waals terms instead, so this figure is 0 for most current systems. A non-zero value marks an older parameter set. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The NPHB pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

definition.val: A relation that groups properties counting what a chemical transformation in a free energy calculation covers, such as the atoms, bonds and angles being changed during the simulation. They set out the scope of the alchemical modification performed. (UNVERIFIED)
In an alchemical free energy calculation, this specifies the total count of bonds being chemically transformed.

comments: The NBPER pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

definition.val: In an alchemical free energy calculation, this specifies the total count of angles being chemically transformed.

comments: The NGPER pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

definition.val: In an alchemical free energy calculation, this specifies the total count of dihedrals being chemically transformed.

comments: The NDPER pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

nodes.lbl: number of total bonds with all atoms in the perturbed group

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of bonds in an alchemical free energy calculation whose 2 atoms both lie in the group being transformed. Such bonds change entirely with the transformation, unlike bonds that cross the boundary of the group and are only partly affected. The distinction determines how each bond is handled along the path. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The MBPER pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

nodes.lbl: number of total angles with all atoms in perturbed groups

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of bond angles in an alchemical free energy calculation whose 3 atoms all lie in the group being transformed. They change entirely with the transformation, unlike angles that straddle its boundary. The distinction determines how each angle is handled along the path. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The MGPER pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

nodes.lbl: number of total dihedrals with all atoms in perturbed groups

definition.val: A relation that gives the number of dihedral angles in an alchemical free energy calculation whose 4 atoms all lie in the group being transformed. They change entirely with the transformation, unlike dihedrals that straddle its boundary. The distinction determines how each dihedral is handled along the path. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: The MDPER pointer in an AMBER prmtop topology file.

definition.val: A relation that groups properties describing the overall state or the main qualitative features of a molecular system, such as yes-or-no flags and short textual descriptions of its composition and setup. They give high-level context about what kind of simulation it is. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that states whether a molecular system contains at least 1 ligand molecule. It marks at a glance which simulations concern binding rather than a molecule on its own. No field in a topology file records this, so it has to be stated by whoever describes the system. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that states whether salt ions were added to a system beyond the counterions needed to make it neutral. Added salt sets the ionic strength, which changes how strongly charges are screened and how molecules interact. No field in a topology file records this, so it has to be stated by whoever describes the system. (UNVERIFIED)

A boolean descriptor indicating whether the molecular system houses an explicit lipid bilayer, rather than just an aqueous or implicit solvent environment. This is a higher-level descriptor not directly present in the prmtop pointers.

A relation that states whether the starting structure contained more than one arrangement for some part of the molecule. Crystal structures often record 2 positions for a flexible side chain, and which was used changes what the simulation began from. No field in a topology file records this, so it has to be stated by whoever describes the system. (UNVERIFIED)

A textual description of the types, proportions and spatial arrangements of different lipid molecules used to construct a biological membrane. This is a higher-level descriptor not directly present in the prmtop pointers.

A numerical or string representation of the relative amounts of different lipid types in a membrane. For example, a value of "3:1" could describe a mixture of two different lipids. This provides a semiquantitative description of the membrane composition.

A relation that associates a molecular system with the index of the first solvent molecule in its ordered list of molecules. In the Amber topology convention this pointer marks where solvent begins, separating solute from solvent. (UNVERIFIED)
A relation that associates a molecular system with how many solvent molecules it contains. It quantifies the amount of solvent used to solvate the solute. (UNVERIFIED)
A relation that associates a trajectory with the atom count recorded in each of its frames. It reflects the size of the coordinate set stored at every saved time point. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular system with a mapping from ion species to the count of ions of each species present. It records the ionic composition used, for example, to neutralize charge or set ionic strength. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: This property stores its value as text, not as a number. The text lists each kind of ion and how many of them there are, for example {"Na+": 12, "Cl-": 10}. That is how the simulation files themselves write it. The other count properties next to this one use plain numbers, because each of them counts a single thing. This one has to count several kinds of ion at the same time, and the ontology has no way yet to say which count belongs to which ion. We looked at two other ways of doing it: making a separate property for every kind of ion, or making a small object that holds one ion and its number. Both would add a lot of work for little gain right now, so we kept the text form. The text itself can be checked later with SHACL, a rule language for checking data files.

definition.val: A relation that associates a molecular system with how many bond-angle terms are defined in its force-field topology. It helps describe the size and complexity of the bonded interaction set. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular system with how many dihedral, or torsion, terms are defined in its force-field topology. It helps describe the size and complexity of the bonded interaction set. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a simulation with how many times a geometric constraint algorithm, such as SHAKE, failed to converge during the run. A nonzero value can signal instability in the integration. (UNVERIFIED)
A relation that associates a simulation run with an indication of whether it finished normally or terminated abnormally. It supports quick screening of runs for successful completion. (UNVERIFIED)
A relation that indicates whether a run was started as a continuation of a previous run rather than from initial conditions. It distinguishes restarted runs from fresh ones. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that indicates whether the atomic coordinates in a trajectory have been translated back into the primary periodic unit cell. It records whether periodic-image wrapping was applied to the stored coordinates. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that indicates whether a simulation uses a combined quantum-mechanics and molecular-mechanics treatment for part of the system. It records whether a region is described at the quantum level while the remainder uses a classical force field. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that indicates whether a run employs self-guided Langevin dynamics, an enhanced sampling scheme that adds a guiding force to accelerate conformational exploration. It records the use of this sampling enhancement. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that indicates whether a spherical solvent cap was applied around a region of interest instead of full periodic solvation. It records the use of a localized, non-periodic solvent boundary. (UNVERIFIED)
A relation that indicates whether periodic box dimension information is present for a molecular system or trajectory. It records whether unit-cell size and shape data are available. (UNVERIFIED)
A relation that indicates whether atomic velocity data are stored alongside coordinates in a file or trajectory. Velocities are needed to seamlessly restart a run. (UNVERIFIED)
OBSOLETE. A relation that records the kind of periodic box used for a molecular system, such as rectangular or truncated octahedral. It identifies the geometry of the periodic unit cell.

comments: Retired 2026-08-13. It duplicated MOLSIM:000297 has periodic box type, which links a molecular simulation system to the class MOLSIM:000032 box type and its five children. This term held the same information as a plain string, so no value could be checked, while the object property points at a real hierarchy that a reasoner can use. Its label also broke the house convention: ten of the eleven data properties ending in flag are yes-or-no values, and this one recorded which box geometry was used.

definition.val: A relation that groups descriptive properties characterizing a molecular dynamics trajectory as a whole, such as its length and coordinate encoding. It serves as an organizing parent for individual trajectory-level metadata relations. (UNVERIFIED)

basicPropertyValues.val: Domain chosen 2026-08-13. This domain asserts something the other grouping properties here do not: anything carrying a child of this property, such as MOLSIM:002138 number of frames, is inferred to be a MOLSIM:001081 simulation trajectory. That is correct if a frame count is only ever recorded about a trajectory. If the source metadata ever records a frame count against a whole run rather than against its trajectory file, the domain should be MOLSIM:000000 molecular dynamics process instead. Confirm against the MDDB records before relying on it.

definition.val: A relation that associates a trajectory with how many saved frames it contains. It reflects how many time points were recorded over the course of the run. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a trajectory or coordinate file with an identifier of the file format used to store its coordinates. It records how the coordinate data are encoded, for example as NetCDF or formatted text. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that groups properties whose values are arrays describing the size and geometry of a molecular system, such as periodic box vectors. It serves as an organizing parent for array-valued structural metadata relations. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular system with an array giving the lengths and angles that define its periodic simulation box. It captures the full geometry of the periodic unit cell. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular system with an array giving the periodic box lengths and angles at the start of a run. It records the initial unit-cell geometry before any volume changes. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that groups properties recording the names and labels assigned to components of a molecular system, such as residue and atom-type names. It serves as an organizing parent for naming-related metadata relations. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular system with the residue name used to identify its solvent in the topology, such as WAT for water. It records the label under which solvent is stored. (UNVERIFIED)
A relation that associates a molecular system with the ordered list of residue names for its constituent residues. It records the per-residue naming as given in the system's topology. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular system with the set of distinct residue names it contains. It summarizes the kinds of residues present without regard to how many times each occurs. (UNVERIFIED)
A relation that associates a molecular system with the set of distinct force-field atom types it uses. It summarizes the range of parameterized atom types present in the topology. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular system with the identifier of the intrinsic radii set used in a generalized Born implicit-solvent calculation. It records which parameterization defines the atomic solvation radii. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that groups properties recording what a simulation or a checking step reported about itself, such as an error message, a warning, or the outcome of a validation check. It gathers the output a run produced about its own progress, as distinct from the settings it was given. (UNVERIFIED)
A relation that associates a simulation or processing step with textual diagnostic output emitted when a fault occurred. It captures the message describing why a run failed. (UNVERIFIED)
A relation that associates a simulation or processing step with a textual warning emitted during execution. Such warnings flag potential problems that did not necessarily stop the run. (UNVERIFIED)
A relation that associates a dataset or run with a non-fatal issue raised during a validation check. It flags a concern found while verifying correctness or consistency. (UNVERIFIED)
A relation that associates a dataset or run with a fault raised during a validation check that caused the check to fail. It records a validation failure. (UNVERIFIED)
A relation that associates a dataset or run with the outcome of a check verifying that its data are mutually consistent. It records whether internal consistency tests passed or failed. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that indicates whether a trajectory or restart file contains atomic coordinate data. Almost every trajectory does, but a file holding only velocities or only forces does not, and reading one expecting coordinates fails. The flag lets a tool decide what a file is good for before opening it. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that indicates whether a trajectory or restart file contains per-atom force data. Forces are rarely written, because they multiply the size of a trajectory and are needed only for specific analyses. Their presence marks a trajectory intended for force analysis or for debugging a force field. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that indicates whether a trajectory file contains per-frame time-stamp data. Without it the frames have an order but no times, so any quantity involving a rate has to assume the interval between them. Stored times also reveal a gap where frames were lost. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that indicates whether a simulation applies NMR-derived restraints or dynamically varying conditions. Such restraints pull the system towards experimental measurements, so the resulting structures reflect the data as well as the force field. A trajectory produced this way must not be treated as a free simulation. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that indicates whether metadata extraction ran in a degraded mode because one or more input files were missing or unreadable. A record produced this way is incomplete rather than wrong, and the missing fields are absent rather than zero. Marking it prevents a partial record being read as a complete one. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that indicates whether a run applies a time-varying target-temperature schedule. A run that heats or cools during its course is not described by a single temperature, so any average taken across it would be meaningless. The flag warns that the run is not at a steady state. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that indicates whether a run applies a time-varying positional-restraint weight schedule. Restraints are commonly released gradually while a system settles, so the strength recorded at the start does not describe the whole run. The flag marks a run in which the restraints changed. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that indicates whether a run applies a time-varying non-bonded cutoff schedule. Changing the cutoff during a run changes how much of each interaction is included, so energies from different parts of the trajectory are not comparable. It is unusual, which is why it is worth recording when it happens. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular system with a descriptive feature or heuristic modification of its force field, such as CMAP support or CHAMBER conversion. These are variations that the name of a force field does not convey, yet they change the energy the system feels. Recording them keeps the force field identifiable from the metadata alone. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular system with a serialized mapping from each residue type to the number of residues of that type present. It says what the system is made of in one value, without a separate term for every residue type. It is stored as text because the set of residue types is open-ended. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a simulation with the complete, serialized set of key-value control parameters parsed from its input file. It preserves every setting, including those MOLSIM has no term for, so nothing in the original input is lost. It is a record for a person to read rather than a structure for a machine to reason over. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a replica-exchange trajectory with the exchanged-coordinate variant detected, such as temperature replica exchange or multi-dimensional replica exchange. What is being exchanged determines what the resulting ensemble means and how the frames may be recombined. A trajectory from one variant cannot be analysed as though it came from another. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a simulation stage with the file path or identifier of the restart file used to initiate it. It is what connects one stage to the one before it, so a chain of stages can be reconstructed after the fact. Without it the stages of a long run are a set of files in no particular order. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that indicates whether the total electrostatic charge of a molecular system is effectively zero, that is, whether the system is electrically neutral. A charged periodic system interacts with its own images in a way that distorts energies, so counter-ions are normally added to neutralise it. A system reported as not neutral needs that explained. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular system with a short human-readable summary of the hydrogen masses observed, such as the mass range and the count of hydrogen atoms, used to describe hydrogen mass repartitioning. Repartitioning moves mass from heavy atoms onto the hydrogens bonded to them, which slows the fastest vibrations and permits a longer timestep. The summary shows at a glance whether it was applied and how far. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a graphics processing unit with the model name of the specific device used to run a simulation, such as the name reported by the CUDA runtime. It explains how long a run took and which software versions it could have used. It should not affect the scientific result, and a difference between devices is a sign that something is wrong. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that indicates whether hydrogen mass repartitioning was inferred from the integration timestep, specifically a timestep of 3 femtoseconds or larger, rather than detected directly from the hydrogen masses in the topology. The inference is a reasonable guess and not a reading, because such a timestep is otherwise unstable. Marking how the value was obtained keeps a guess from being mistaken for a measurement. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a simulation protocol with the total number of integration steps performed across all of its stages. Multiplied by the timestep it gives the total simulated time, which is what determines whether the slow motions of interest could have happened at all. It is the single most useful figure for judging whether a result is likely to be converged. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular system with the number of atoms belonging to its proteins. Proteins are the large chain-like molecules built from amino acids; this reports how many atoms make up all of them together. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular system with the number of atoms belonging to its nucleic acids, that is DNA and RNA taken together. It separates the nucleic acid part of a system from protein, solvent and ions in a single figure. A value of 0 marks a system with no nucleic acid at all. (UNVERIFIED)
A relation that associates a molecular system with the number of atoms belonging to its lipids. Lipids are the fatty molecules that form cell membranes. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular system with the number of atoms that are ions. Ions are individual charged atoms such as sodium or chloride, added to balance charge or set the salt level. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular system with the number of atoms belonging to the solvent (usually water). It differs from number of solvent molecules (002122), which counts whole molecules rather than atoms. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular system with the number of atoms that fall into none of the named categories (protein, nucleic acid, lipid, ion, solvent). It captures leftovers such as small-molecule ligands or cofactors. (UNVERIFIED)
A relation that associates a molecular system with the number of residues in its proteins. A residue is one amino-acid building block of a protein chain. (UNVERIFIED)
A relation that associates a molecular system with the number of residues in its nucleic acids. Here a residue is one nucleotide building block of a DNA or RNA chain. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular system with the number of lipid residues it contains. Each lipid molecule is counted as one residue, so this effectively reports how many lipid molecules make up the membrane or other lipid assembly. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular system with how many nucleosomes it contains. A nucleosome is the basic repeating unit of chromatin, a stretch of DNA wound around a core of histone proteins. (UNVERIFIED)

nodes.lbl: number of nucleotides per DNA strand

definition.val: A relation that associates the system with the length of a DNA strand, measured as the number of nucleotide bases it contains. Because a system can contain several strands, this may be recorded once per strand. (UNVERIFIED)
A relation that records the box angles as an ordered list of values (e.g. α, β, γ). It stores the raw angle data read from or written to a simulation file. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that states whether a saved trajectory includes the atomic positions (the 3-D coordinates of every atom over time). Positions are the most basic trajectory data and are almost always present. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that states whether a saved trajectory includes the forces acting on each atom over time. Forces are optional extra data, useful for example when training machine-learning models. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that records the version number of a piece of software, such as an MD engine (for example, version 2024.1). Recording the version makes a simulation reproducible, because software behaviour can change between versions. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that records whether a simulated system includes an antibody, a Y-shaped immune protein that recognises and sticks to a specific target such as a virus. Antibodies are large and their binding surfaces are flexible loops, so simulating one is harder than simulating a compact protein of the same size. The flag marks the systems where that difficulty applies. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that records whether a simulated system includes a nanobody, a very small, single-piece version of an antibody, originally from animals such as llamas, used as a compact binding tool. Being roughly a tenth the size of an antibody, it is within reach of simulations that a full antibody is not. It binds through a single long loop rather than a pair of surfaces. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that records whether the system includes a linker histone, such as histone H1, an extra histone that clamps the DNA where it enters and leaves the spool. It is not part of the spool itself and is often missing from experimental structures, so its presence changes what a simulation represents. Including it stiffens the DNA at the entry and exit points. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that records whether the histone proteins still have their flexible tails, the floppy ends that stick out from the spool and are often chemically marked to control gene activity. The tails are disordered, so they are frequently cut from a structure to make it easier to simulate. Removing them also removes the part that most of the biology depends on. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that groups properties recording what a simulation run was given to start from, such as the settings parsed from its input file or the restart file it continued from. It covers the input side of a run, as distinct from what the run reported about itself. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular dynamics process with the file path or identifier of the topology file defining the simulated system, such as an AMBER prmtop file or a GROMACS top file. The topology file states which atoms are present, how they are bonded, which parameters they were assigned, and which chemical states were assumed when the system was built. (UNVERIFIED)

basicPropertyValues.val: MOLSIM records the composition of a simulated system at the system level and points at the topology and coordinate files for the per-residue detail, rather than restating that detail term by term. This is why there is no vocabulary for individual histidine or cysteine states: those are decided per residue and per atom, and the topology file states them exactly. Paired with MOLSIM:002257 has coordinate file path, which records the starting positions.

definition.val: A relation that associates a molecular dynamics process with the file path or identifier of the coordinate file holding the starting position of every atom, such as an AMBER inpcrd or rst7 file or a GROMACS gro file. Together with the topology file it fixes the exact system state a run began from. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular simulation system with any solvent added alongside water, such as urea, glycerol or an alcohol. A cosolvent changes how the solute behaves, and a record that omits it describes a different system from the one that was run. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: This property stores its value as text, because a system may contain more than 1 cosolvent and each may carry a concentration. Values look like "urea 8 M" or "glycerol 30 percent, DMSO 5 percent". Checking the text follows a fixed shape is a job for SHACL rather than OWL.

basicPropertyValues.val: Holds text rather than pointing at a named class for each substance, and that is a deliberate choice rather than a shortcut. Pointing at named classes would need MOLSIM classes for urea, glycerol, DMSO and every other cosolvent, which is a chemistry vocabulary that ChEBI already provides with roughly 190,000 terms. The ChEBI import was removed on 2026-08-24 because all 189 classes it delivered were unreferenced, and the agreed approach records what a system is made of at the system level while pointing at the topology file for the per-residue chemical detail. The cost of the text form is real: urea, Urea, URE and 8M urea are the same substance and different strings, so a search by substance is unreliable. Revisit only when a specific record must be queried by substance rather than read by a person. The fix then is to import the few named ChEBI terms actually needed, bounded so that no ancestors arrive with them, and change this property to point at those. The same reasoning applies to the data properties MOLSIM:001161 lipid composition and MOLSIM:001162 lipid ratio, which also hold text.

definition.val: A relation that records whether the two layers of a simulated membrane hold the same mixture of lipids as each other. Real cell membranes are usually different on their two sides, so whether a simulation copied that difference or ignored it changes what the results can be said to show. (UNVERIFIED)

A relation that associates a molecular simulation system with the size of its membrane patch in the plane of the membrane. The patch must be wide enough that a protein does not feel its own periodic copy across the boundary, so the size limits which conclusions the simulation can support. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: This property stores its value as text, because the size has 2 numbers and a unit. Values look like "9.5 x 9.5 nm" or "120 x 95 angstrom". It carries no unit restriction for the same reason MOLSIM:001213 periodic box dimensions carries none: the unit and value pattern describes a single number, and a patch size is two. A single length in this domain does take that pattern, as MOLSIM:001875 membrane width does. Checking the text follows a fixed shape is a job for SHACL rather than OWL.

definition.val: A relation that associates a molecular simulation system with the rule used to delete lipids that overlapped the protein when the membrane was built. Placing a protein into a lipid patch always leaves some lipids sitting where the protein is, and the rule chosen for removing them decides how many lipids the finished system holds. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: This property stores its value as text, because the rule is usually a short description rather than a single number. Values look like "lipids with any atom within 0.6 nm of the protein were deleted" or "removed by the InflateGRO procedure". Checking the text follows a fixed shape is a job for SHACL rather than OWL.

definition.val: The term was initially used in an attempt to structure part of the ontology, but in retrospect failed to do a good job.
Class has all its metadata, but is either not guaranteed to be in its final location in the asserted IS_A hierarchy or refers to another class that is not complete.
The term was created to ease viewing/sorting terms for development purposes, but will not be included in a release.

Class has undergone final review, is ready for use, and will be included in the next release. Any class lacking "ready_for_release" should be considered likely to change place in hierarchy, have its definition refined, or be obsoleted in the next release.  Those classes deemed "ready_for_release" will also derived from a chain of ancestor classes that are also "ready_for_release."
Class is being worked on; however, the metadata (including definition) are not complete or sufficiently clear to the branch editors.
Nothing done yet beyond assigning a unique class ID and proposing a preferred term.
All definitions, placement in the asserted IS_A hierarchy and required minimal metadata are complete. The class is awaiting a final review by someone other than the term editor.
The term was created to temporarily stand in for a semantic purpose, but is no longer needed, typically due to another permanent term being defined.
The term has been combined with one or more other terms to create a more encompassing (merged) term.
The term has been replaced by a term imported from another ontology.
The term has been split into two or more new terms.

A named class expression is a logical expression that is given a name. The name can be used in place of the expression.

definition.val: Terms with this status should eventually replaced with a term from another ontology.
A term that is metadata complete, has been reviewed, and problems have been identified that require discussion before release. Such a term requires editor note(s) to identify the outstanding issues.

A protein structural database that is the single worldwide archive for experimentally determined 3-dimensional structures of large biological molecules, including proteins, nucleic acids and their complexes. Nearly every simulation of a biological molecule begins with a structure taken from it. Its accession codes are the standard way a structure is cited. (UNVERIFIED)

A protein structural database that is the European member of the worldwide Protein Data Bank partnership, holding the same archive and adding its own search and analysis tools. The 3 regional members share one set of entries, so a structure deposited at any of them appears at all. What differs is the interface and the services built on top. (UNVERIFIED)

A founding member of the Worldwide Protein Data Bank (wwPDB) organization, serving as the Asian regional center for the PDB. PDBj collects, processes, and disseminates macromolecular structure data, and develops tools and resources for structural biology research in Japan and globally. (UNVERIFIED)

A pictorial database that provides an at-a-glance overview of the contents of each 3D macromolecular structure deposited in the Protein Data Bank (PDB). PDBsum presents schematic diagrams of molecular interactions, protein domains, ligand binding sites, and other structural features. It is a useful tool for quickly understanding PDB entries. (UNVERIFIED)

A nucleic acid structural database archiving experimentally determined 3-dimensional structures of DNA, RNA and their complexes. It describes structures in terms specific to nucleic acids, such as base pairing and backbone conformation, which a general structure archive does not. It is where nucleic acid geometry is looked up rather than derived. (UNVERIFIED)

An electron microscopy database that is the main public archive for 3-dimensional density maps of biomolecular complexes and subcellular structures. A map from this source shows shape at a resolution that may be too low to place individual atoms, which is why an atomic model is deposited separately. The 2 together are what a cryogenic electron microscopy study produces. (UNVERIFIED)

An electron microscopy database holding the raw 2-dimensional image data, including movies and tilt series, from which 3-dimensional maps were reconstructed. Keeping the raw images allows a reconstruction to be repeated or improved as methods advance. It is the layer beneath the density map archive. (UNVERIFIED)

The NIH genetic sequence database, an annotated collection of all publicly available DNA sequences, maintained by the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI). As part of the INSDC, GenBank is a foundational resource for molecular biology, genomics, and evolutionary studies worldwide. (UNVERIFIED)

A knowledge-based database of protein sequences together with what is known about each protein's function, structure and modifications. It was formed by joining 3 earlier collections and is the reference most protein identifiers point at. It has a manually reviewed section and a much larger automatically annotated one. (UNVERIFIED)

A nucleic acid sequence database covering raw sequencing reads, assembled sequences and their annotations, from organisms of every kind. It is the European member of a 3-way partnership whose members exchange records daily, so a sequence deposited at one appears at all. Which one holds a record therefore says where it was deposited, not where it can be found. (UNVERIFIED)

A nucleic acid sequence database that is the Japanese member of the same 3-way partnership as the European and American archives. The 3 exchange records daily and hold the same content. It is the deposition route for work done in its region. (UNVERIFIED)

The manually annotated and reviewed section of the UniProt Knowledgebase (UniProtKB). Swiss-Prot entries contain high-quality protein sequence information, detailed functional annotations, and extensive cross-references, derived from literature and curator evaluation. It represents the gold standard for protein annotation. (UNVERIFIED)

The computationally annotated section of the UniProt Knowledgebase (UniProtKB), containing protein sequences that are not yet manually curated. TrEMBL entries are largely derived from the translation of coding sequences in nucleotide sequence databases and are automatically annotated. It provides broad sequence coverage. (UNVERIFIED)

The NCBI Reference Sequence (RefSeq) collection for protein data, offering a curated, non-redundant set of protein sequences, often linked to corresponding nucleotide sequences and genomic annotations. RefSeq proteins serve as stable reference points for protein identification, annotation, and comparative analysis. (UNVERIFIED)

A protein sequence database that produced one of the first curated collections of protein sequences, beginning in the 1960s. Its own collection is no longer maintained separately, having been merged into the UniProt Knowledgebase. It remains cited because a great deal of older literature refers to its identifiers. (UNVERIFIED)

The NCBI Reference Sequence (RefSeq) collection for nucleotide data, providing a comprehensive, integrated, non-redundant, and well-annotated set of sequences for chromosomes, genomic regions, transcripts, and RNAs. RefSeq aims to provide stable reference sequences for various organisms. It is a critical resource for genomics and gene annotation. (UNVERIFIED)

A public repository within PubChem that contains validated chemical structure information for small molecules, including their identifiers, properties, and links to related information. PubChem Compound is a comprehensive resource for chemical information and a key component of the PubChem suite. (UNVERIFIED)

A chemical structure database and ontology covering small molecules that take part in biological processes, as products, reactants or regulators. Being an ontology as well as a dictionary, it records how compounds relate to one another rather than only listing them. MOLSIM maps to it and does not import it, because its hierarchy is far deeper than this field needs. (UNVERIFIED)

A free database of commercially available chemical compounds prepared in ready-to-dock, 3D formats for virtual screening and computational drug discovery. ZINC20 contains millions of purchasable compounds with annotated properties, facilitating large-scale ligand docking and cheminformatics studies. (UNVERIFIED)

A comprehensive, freely accessible online database containing detailed information on drugs, drug targets, drug interactions, and drug metabolism. It combines detailed drug data with comprehensive drug target information, making it a vital resource for pharmacology, medicinal chemistry, and pharmaceutical research. (UNVERIFIED)

A free chemical structure database providing fast access to over millions of structures, properties, and associated information from various sources. It allows users to search by chemical name, synonym, trade name, registry number, or structure. ChemSpider is a comprehensive resource for chemists and researchers needing chemical information. (UNVERIFIED)

A drug information database recording the protein and nucleic acid targets that drugs act on, the drugs directed at each, and the diseases involved. It is organised around the target rather than the compound. It is used to find what has already been tried against a protein before a new study is designed. (UNVERIFIED)

A website operated by the U.S. National Library of Medicine (NLM) that provides high-quality information about marketed drugs, including FDA-approved drug labels (package inserts). It offers comprehensive information for healthcare providers and the public on drug ingredients, indications, dosage, warnings, and adverse reactions. (UNVERIFIED)

A manually curated, large-scale database of bioactive drug-like small molecules and their quantitative bioactivity data against drug targets (primarily proteins). It brings together chemical, bioactivity, and genomic data to aid the translation of genomic information into effective new drugs. ChEMBL is a critical resource for drug discovery, pharmacology, and medicinal chemistry. (UNVERIFIED)

A spectroscopic database holding mass spectrometry datasets, chiefly from proteomics experiments. It stores the measurements themselves rather than conclusions drawn from them, so an analysis can be repeated. It is one of the archives a proteomics study is expected to deposit in. (UNVERIFIED)

An integrated spectral database system for organic compounds, maintained by the National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology (AIST), Japan. SDBS contains NMR (1H, 13C), mass spectra, IR, Raman, and ESR spectra for a large number of organic compounds. It is a valuable resource for chemical identification and structural elucidation. (UNVERIFIED)

An NMR data repository collecting nuclear magnetic resonance measurements on biological macromolecules and metabolites, including assigned chemical shifts, coupling constants and relaxation data. Those quantities are what a simulated structure or trajectory is compared against. It is the NMR counterpart of the structure archives. (UNVERIFIED)

An NMR data repository specialising in assigned chemical shifts for complex carbohydrates and their complexes. Carbohydrates are poorly covered by the general NMR archives, because their signals overlap heavily and their assignment is difficult. It exists to hold the assignments that do get made. (UNVERIFIED)

A database that integrates predictive signatures for protein families, domains, and functional sites from multiple member databases (e.g., Pfam, PROSITE, SMART, CDD, CATH, SCOP). InterPro provides a comprehensive overview of protein sequence features, aiding in functional annotation and comparative analysis. It is a powerful tool for protein characterization. (UNVERIFIED)

A large collection of protein families, each represented by multiple sequence alignments and hidden Markov models (HMMs). Pfam is used to identify conserved domains and families in protein sequences, providing insights into their function and evolutionary relationships. It is a widely used resource for protein sequence annotation. (UNVERIFIED)

A web-based resource used for the identification and annotation of genetically mobile domains and the analysis of domain architectures in proteins. SMART contains manually curated models for hundreds of domains involved in signaling, extracellular functions, and chromatin regulation. It is a valuable tool for protein sequence analysis and functional prediction. (UNVERIFIED)

A database of protein domains, families, and functional sites, characterized by patterns (regular expressions) or profiles (position-specific scoring matrices) derived from multiple sequence alignments. PROSITE is used to identify known motifs and domains in protein sequences, aiding in functional prediction. It is part of the SIB ExPASy server. (UNVERIFIED)

A protein family and domain database holding curated models of protein domains, together with models imported from other collections. Searching a sequence against it identifies which known domains a protein contains. That is usually the first step in deciding what part of a protein to simulate. (UNVERIFIED)

A database that provides a detailed and comprehensive hierarchical classification of protein structural domains based on their evolutionary relationships and structural similarities. SCOP2 builds upon the original SCOP, aiming to provide a more automated and comprehensive classification. It is a key resource for understanding protein structure and evolution. (UNVERIFIED)

A structural classification database that sorts protein domains taken from experimental structures into a hierarchy of 4 levels, from broad shape down to evolutionary relationship. The 4 levels are what its name enumerates. It is used to find structurally similar proteins when sequence similarity is too weak to detect. (UNVERIFIED)

A structural classification database that groups protein domains primarily by evolutionary relationship rather than by shape. It emphasises distant relationships that a purely structural comparison would miss. It is updated continuously as new structures appear, where some classifications are revised in releases. (UNVERIFIED)

A collection of manually drawn pathway maps representing current knowledge on molecular interaction and reaction networks for metabolism, genetic information processing, environmental information processing, cellular processes, organismal systems, and human diseases. KEGG Pathway is part of the larger Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) resource. It is widely used for pathway analysis and systems biology. (UNVERIFIED)

A free, open-source, curated, and peer-reviewed pathway database that provides detailed information on human biological pathways and processes. Reactome uses a hierarchical organization to describe molecular events, from individual reactions to complex pathways, linking genes, proteins, and small molecules. It is a key resource for systems biology and pathway analysis. (UNVERIFIED)

A collection of thousands of Pathway/Genome Databases (PGDBs), each describing the genome and metabolic pathways of a specific organism, plus a multi-organism pathway database (MetaCyc). BioCyc provides curated information on genes, enzymes, metabolites, and reactions, facilitating comparative genomics and metabolic network analysis. It is a key resource for systems biology. (UNVERIFIED)

A community-curated, open, and collaborative platform for biological pathway diagrams. WikiPathways allows researchers to contribute, edit, and share pathway information, fostering a dynamic and up-to-date collection of pathway models across various species. It promotes open access to pathway knowledge. (UNVERIFIED)

A public, web-accessible database focusing on measured binding affinities of interactions between proteins (considered as drug targets) and small, drug-like molecules. It primarily contains data from enzyme assays, isothermal titration calorimetry, and surface plasmon resonance. BindingDB is a valuable resource for drug discovery, cheminformatics, and validating computational predictions. (UNVERIFIED)

A public repository within PubChem that stores descriptions and results of biological screening assays on chemical substances, typically from high-throughput screening programs. PubChem BioAssay links chemical structures to their biological activities, providing valuable data for drug discovery and chemical biology. (UNVERIFIED)

A bioactivity database, curated by experts, of pharmacological targets such as receptors, ion channels, enzymes and transporters, together with the drugs and ligands that act on them. Its entries are written and checked by specialists in each target family rather than gathered automatically. That makes it smaller than the automatically assembled collections and more reliable per entry. (UNVERIFIED)

A discovery platform integrating and standardizing data on gene-disease associations (GDAs) and variant-disease associations (VDAs) from multiple public repositories and scientific literature. DisGeNET provides scores to rank these associations and tools for their analysis and interpretation. It is a valuable resource for studying the genetic basis of human diseases. (UNVERIFIED)

A knowledge-based database cataloguing human genes and the inherited disorders and traits associated with them. It is organised around the link between a gene and the effects of altering it, rather than around sequences. It is how a mutation being simulated is connected to a clinical consequence. (UNVERIFIED)

A general-purpose open-access repository operated by CERN and OpenAIRE, allowing researchers in all disciplines to deposit research outputs, including datasets, software, publications, and figures. Zenodo assigns DOIs to uploads, making them citable and discoverable. It supports FAIR data principles. (UNVERIFIED)

A general-purpose, curated repository that makes the data underlying scientific and medical publications discoverable, freely reusable, and citable. Dryad provides a platform for researchers to archive and share diverse datasets associated with their research articles. It promotes open science and data reproducibility. (UNVERIFIED)

A general-purpose online digital repository where researchers can preserve and share their research outputs, including figures, datasets, images, and code. Figshare allows users to make their work citable and discoverable, supporting open science practices across various disciplines. (UNVERIFIED)

A simulation data repository, based in Europe, for storing and sharing biomolecular simulation data. It accepts trajectories together with the metadata describing how they were produced, which is what makes a deposited trajectory reusable. MOLSIM exists in large part to give that metadata a shared vocabulary. (UNVERIFIED)

A publicly accessible database designed to store, search, and analyze biomolecular simulation data, including trajectories, input parameters, and analysis results. It aims to promote reproducibility, data sharing, and re-use of simulation data within the molecular modeling community. BioSimDB facilitates the discovery and comparison of simulation studies. (UNVERIFIED)

A database and web server that provides a collection of pre-equilibrated molecular dynamics simulations of proteins, particularly focusing on pharmaceutically relevant targets. MoDEL aims to offer ready-to-use starting points for further simulation studies, such as ligand binding or conformational analysis. (UNVERIFIED)

comments: Distinct from the class 'model' (MOLSIM:000006), which it resembles only in spelling: this is a named simulation data repository, that is a general kind of representation. Case-insensitive lexical matching conflates the two, so prefer the synonym 'MoDEL database' when matching.

definition.val: A web server and platform designed for sharing, visualizing, and analyzing molecular dynamics (MD) simulation trajectories directly in a web browser. MDsrv allows researchers to easily disseminate their MD data and provides interactive tools for common trajectory analyses without requiring local software installation. (UNVERIFIED)

A prototype deposition and archiving system for structural models of biomolecular systems determined using integrative or hybrid (I/H) methods, which combine data from various experimental techniques and computational approaches. PDB-Dev aims to establish standards for archiving these complex structural models. (UNVERIFIED)

A comprehensive repository providing open access to millions of high-accuracy protein structure predictions generated by DeepMind's AlphaFold AI system. It significantly expands structural coverage of known protein sequences, offering valuable models for proteins lacking experimental structures. This database is a key resource for structural biology and drug discovery. (UNVERIFIED)

A database of continuously updated, high-quality 3D protein structure models generated by the SWISS-MODEL homology modeling pipeline. It provides access to pre-computed models for a large number of protein sequences, particularly those from model organisms and UniProtKB. It is a key resource for obtaining theoretical protein models. (UNVERIFIED)

A predicted structure repository holding several hundred million protein structure predictions, generated by a language model trained on protein sequences. Its scale comes from predicting directly from sequence without searching for related structures, which is far faster than earlier methods. Its predictions are less accurate than those from methods that do search, and cover sequences those methods have never been run on. (UNVERIFIED)

A public repository for archiving and distributing 3D structural models of biomacromolecules, particularly those generated by computational methods that are not eligible for deposition in the PDB. ModelArchive supports the FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) principles for theoretical models. (UNVERIFIED)

A database for cross-species, cross-technique metabolomics experiments and derived information, maintained at EMBL-EBI. MetaboLights archives metadata about studies, raw experimental data, and processed metabolite identifications and quantifications. It is a key repository for the metabolomics community. (UNVERIFIED)

A metabolomics repository and analysis platform for mass spectrometry data on natural products, which groups related compounds by the similarity of their spectra. Grouping this way identifies compounds that no reference library contains, by their resemblance to ones it does. Its reference spectra are contributed and curated by its users. (UNVERIFIED)

synonyms.val: Global Natural Products Social Molecular Networking

definition.val: A public repository for metabolomics data and metadata, part of the NIH Common Fund's Metabolomics Program. It serves as a national and international data repository and coordinating center, providing tools for data analysis, visualization, and integration with other omics data. (UNVERIFIED)

A free search engine primarily accessing the MEDLINE database of references and abstracts on life sciences and biomedical topics, maintained by the U.S. National Library of Medicine (NLM) at the National Institutes of Health (NIH). PubMed is the foremost resource for searching biomedical literature. (UNVERIFIED)

A large abstract and citation database of peer-reviewed literature: scientific journals, books, and conference proceedings, owned by Elsevier. Scopus provides tools for tracking, analyzing, and visualizing research output across various disciplines. It is a major competitor to Web of Science for literature searching and citation analysis. (UNVERIFIED)

A multidisciplinary citation indexing service and database platform owned by Clarivate Analytics. Web of Science provides access to multiple databases covering scholarly journals, books, conference proceedings, and patents, offering comprehensive citation data and research analytics. It is a major tool for literature discovery and impact assessment. (UNVERIFIED)

A freely accessible web search engine that indexes the full text or metadata of scholarly literature across an array of publishing formats and disciplines. While not a curated database, it serves as a primary discovery tool for finding academic papers, theses, books, and abstracts. It is widely used by researchers for literature searches. (UNVERIFIED)

The small molecule structural database that serves as the primary repository for experimentally determined three-dimensional crystal structures of small organic and metal-organic molecules. It provides high-quality reference geometries used for validating force fields and for obtaining starting structures in computational studies. (UNVERIFIED)
OBSOLETE. A redundant untyped individual that duplicated the class 'omni-path' (MOLSIM:001949). It should not be used; use that class instead.

comments: Obsoleted: redundant untyped individual duplicating the class 'omni-path' (MOLSIM_001949), which is the concept to use instead.

definition.val: The file format convention denoted by the string AMBERRESTART in a NetCDF file's global Conventions attribute, designating the file as an AMBER restart or state file. NetCDF is a general container, so the same file extension can hold quite different contents and only this attribute says which. A reader that ignores it will happily open a restart file as though it were a trajectory. (UNVERIFIED)

The file format convention denoted by the string AMBER in a NetCDF file's global Conventions attribute, designating the file as an AMBER coordinate trajectory. It is the counterpart of the restart convention and distinguishes a file of many frames from a file holding one state. The distinction cannot be made from the file extension alone. (UNVERIFIED)

The system classification label assigned to a molecular system composed of a protein receptor, a small-molecule ligand, and explicit water molecules. It is the commonest arrangement in binding studies, which is why it has a label of its own. Knowing a system is of this kind says what analyses will apply to it before any file is opened. (UNVERIFIED)

The hydrogen detection strategy that identifies hydrogen atoms by testing whether an atom's atomic number is exactly one, used when applying or detecting hydrogen mass repartitioning. It is the reliable test, because atomic number is a physical fact recorded in the topology. It fails only where the topology omits atomic numbers, which is why a name-based fallback exists. (UNVERIFIED)

The hydrogen detection strategy that identifies hydrogen atoms by testing whether an atom's name begins with the letter H, used when applying or detecting hydrogen mass repartitioning. It is a fallback for topologies that do not record atomic numbers. It is not reliable: helium, hafnium and mercury also begin with H, and some naming conventions put a digit first. (UNVERIFIED)
The term was added to the ontology on the assumption it was in scope, but it turned out later that it was not.
The term was added to the ontology on the assumption it was a valid domain entity, but it turns out the entity does not exist in reality.
The concise, meaningful, and human-friendly name for a class or property preferred by the ontology developers. (US-English)

A phrase describing how a term should be used and/or a citation to a work which uses it. May also include other kinds of examples that facilitate immediate understanding, such as widely know prototypes or instances of a class, or cases where a relation is said to hold.
The official definition, explaining the meaning of a class or property. Shall be Aristotelian, formalized and normalized. Can be augmented with colloquial definitions.

basicPropertyValues.val:
2012-04-05: 
Barry Smith

The official OBI definition, explaining the meaning of a class or property: 'Shall be Aristotelian, formalized and normalized. Can be augmented with colloquial definitions'  is terrible.

Can you fix to something like:

A statement of necessary and sufficient conditions explaining the meaning of an expression referring to a class or property.

Alan Ruttenberg

Your proposed definition is a reasonable candidate, except that it is very common that necessary and sufficient conditions are not given. Mostly they are necessary, occasionally they are necessary and sufficient or just sufficient. Often they use terms that are not themselves defined and so they effectively can't be evaluated by those criteria. 

On the specifics of the proposed definition:

We don't have definitions of 'meaning' or 'expression' or 'property'. For 'reference' in the intended sense I think we use the term 'denotation'. For 'expression', I think we you mean symbol, or identifier. For 'meaning' it differs for class and property. For class we want documentation that let's the intended reader determine whether an entity is instance of the class, or not. For property we want documentation that let's the intended reader determine, given a pair of potential relata, whether the assertion that the relation holds is true. The 'intended reader' part suggests that we also specify who, we expect, would be able to understand the definition, and also generalizes over human and computer reader to include textual and logical definition. 

Personally, I am more comfortable weakening definition to documentation, with instructions as to what is desirable. 

We also have the outstanding issue of how to aim different definitions to different audiences. A clinical audience reading chebi wants a different sort of definition documentation/definition from a chemistry trained audience, and similarly there is a need for a definition that is adequate for an ontologist to work with.

definition.val: An administrative note intended for its editor. It may not be included in the publication version of the ontology, so it should contain nothing necessary for end users to understand the ontology.

Name of editor entering the term in the file. The term editor is a point of contact for information regarding the term. The term editor may be, but is not always, the author of the definition, which may have been worked upon by several people

Formal citation, e.g. identifier in external database to indicate / attribute source(s) for the definition. Free text indicate / attribute source(s) for the definition. EXAMPLE: Author Name, URI, MeSH Term C04, PUBMED ID, Wiki uri on 31.01.2007

definition.val: Use on obsolete terms, relating the term to another term that can be used as a substitute

comments: Add as annotation triples in the granting ontology

definition.val: A relation that records the name a piece of simulation software uses for the concept this term names, as it appears in that software's input file, output file or command line. The software the name belongs to is given by annotating the statement itself with dcterms:source, so one property serves every program rather than needing one property per program. (UNVERIFIED)
an alternative term used for STATO statistical ontology and ISA team
a R command syntax or link to a R documentation in support of Statistical Ontology Classes or Data Transformations
an annotation property to provide a canonical command to invoke a method implementation using Python programming language
